body.title: Thinking like a director
body.mdx:
A short film doesn't move you because the idea was good — it moves you because of the colors, the camera angles, the storytelling. That's the whole thesis of this course: you're not learning to prompt an AI film, you're learning to think like the director who decides what every shot should feel like before a single frame gets generated.

The film behind this course — a football drama about a striker replaying the penalty he missed — was built entirely inside Higgsfield AI, with Claude Fable 5 writing the screenplay and Seedance 2.0 4K shooting every scene. Every technique in the lessons that follow — locking a character on a grey reference sheet, framing a 3/4 angle for depth, cutting on a Dutch angle to build tension, timing a whip pan or a speed ramp — exists to serve one thing: making an AI-generated shot read as *directed*, not generated.

> [!TIP]
> Before you touch a single prompt, watch the finished film once as an audience member, not a builder. Notice what makes you feel something — that's the shot list you're about to learn to write.
